/-!
# Eden's conjecture

Eden's conjecture states that the supremum of the local Lyapunov dimensions on the global
attractor of a smooth dynamical system is achieved on a stationary point or an unstable periodic
orbit embedded into the attractor. It was proposed by Alp Eden in 1987.

We follow the finite-dimensional setting of Kuznetsov (2016). A smooth dynamical system is a
semiflow $\{\varphi^t\}_{t \ge 0}$ on a finite-dimensional real inner product space $E$ of
dimension $n$ whose time-$t$ maps are continuously differentiable. For $u \in E$ and $t \ge 0$,
let $\sigma_1(t, u) \ge \dots \ge \sigma_n(t, u) \ge 0$ be the singular values of
$D\varphi^t(u)$ and, for $d \in [0, n]$, let
$$\omega_d(D\varphi^t(u)) = \sigma_1(t, u) \cdots \sigma_{\lfloor d \rfloor}(t, u)\,
  \sigma_{\lfloor d \rfloor + 1}(t, u)^{d - \lfloor d \rfloor}$$
be the singular value function. The (infinite-time) local Lyapunov dimension of Eden at $u$ is
$$\dim_{\rm L}^{\rm E}(u) = \inf\{d \in [0, n] :
  \limsup_{t \to +\infty} \big(\omega_d(D\varphi^t(u))\big)^{1/t} < 1\},$$
with the convention that it equals $n$ when no such $d$ exists.

A global attractor is a compact set $K$ which is strictly invariant, $\varphi^t(K) = K$ for all
$t \ge 0$, and which attracts every bounded set.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Eden's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- A. Eden, *An abstract theory of L-exponents with applications to dimension analysis*,
  PhD thesis, Indiana University (1989), p. 98, Question 1.
- A. Eden, *Local Lyapunov exponents and a local estimate of Hausdorff dimension*,
  Modélisation Mathématique et Analyse Numérique 23 (1989),
  [doi:10.1051/m2an/1989230304051](https://doi.org/10.1051/m2an/1989230304051).
- N. V. Kuznetsov, *The Lyapunov dimension and its estimation via the Leonov method*,
  Physics Letters A 380 (2016), [arXiv:1602.05410](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.05410).
-/

blocks.code:
noncomputable def singularValueFunction (A : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) (d : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∏ i ∈ Finset.range ⌊d⌋₊, singularValue A i) * singularValue A ⌊d⌋₊ ^ (d - ⌊d⌋₊)
blocks.docstring:
The singular value function of order `d` of a linear map `A` with singular values
`σ₁ ≥ σ₂ ≥ ⋯ ≥ σₙ`: for `d ∈ [0, n]` it is
`ω_d(A) = σ₁ ⋯ σ_{⌊d⌋} σ_{⌊d⌋ + 1} ^ (d - ⌊d⌋)`, so that `ω_0(A) = 1` and `ω_n(A) = |det A|`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No analogue in Mathlib (exterior-power operator norms are also unavailable).
justification.name: EdensConjecture.singularValueFunction
justification.why_needed: The singular value function ω_d(A) = σ₁⋯σ_{⌊d⌋} σ_{⌊d⌋+1}^{d-⌊d⌋} of real order d, central to the Douady–Oesterlé/Eden/Kuznetsov Lyapunov dimension, is absent from Mathlib.

noncomputable def localLyapunovDim (φ : Flow ℝ≥0 E) (u : E) : ℝ :=
  sInf {d ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (Module.finrank ℝ E) | d = Module.finrank ℝ E ∨
    limsup (fun t : ℝ≥0 => ENNReal.ofReal
      (singularValueFunction (fderiv ℝ (φ t) u : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) d ^ (1 / (t : ℝ)))) atTop < 1}
blocks.docstring:
The (infinite-time) local Lyapunov dimension in the sense of Eden of a semiflow `φ` on an
`n`-dimensional space at the point `u`:
$$\dim_{\rm L}^{\rm E}(u) = \inf\{d \in [0, n] :
  \limsup_{t \to +\infty} \big(\omega_d(D\varphi^t(u))\big)^{1/t} < 1\},$$
where `ω_d` is the singular value function and `Dφᵗ(u)` is the derivative of the time-`t` map
at `u`. The `limsup` is taken in `[0, ∞]`. If no `d ∈ [0, n]` satisfies the condition, the
dimension is `n`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing on Lyapunov exponents/dimensions in Mathlib; `Filter.limsup`, `fderiv`, `Flow` are used as building blocks.

justification.why_needed: Eden's infinite-time local Lyapunov dimension inf{d ∈ [0,n] : limsup ω_d(Dφᵗ(u))^{1/t} < 1} (with value n if empty) does not exist in Mathlib or the repo.

@[category API, AMS 37]
theorem localLyapunovDim_mem_Icc (φ : Flow ℝ≥0 E) (u : E) :
    localLyapunovDim φ u ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (Module.finrank ℝ E) := by
  have hmem : (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) ∈ {d ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (Module.finrank ℝ E) |
      d = Module.finrank ℝ E ∨ limsup (fun t : ℝ≥0 => ENNReal.ofReal
        (singularValueFunction (fderiv ℝ (φ t) u : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) d ^ (1 / (t : ℝ)))) atTop < 1} :=
    ⟨⟨by positivity, le_rfl⟩, Or.inl rfl⟩
  exact ⟨le_csInf ⟨_, hmem⟩ fun d hd => hd.1.1, csInf_le ⟨0, fun d hd => hd.1.1⟩ hmem⟩
blocks.docstring: The local Lyapunov dimension takes values in `[0, n]`.

blocks.code:
structure IsGlobalAttractor (φ : Flow ℝ≥0 E) (K : Set E) : Prop where
  isCompact : IsCompact K
  image_eq : ∀ t, φ t '' K = K
  attracts : ∀ B : Set E, Bornology.IsBounded B →
    ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ t in atTop, φ t '' B ⊆ thickening ε K
blocks.docstring:
`K` is the global attractor of the semiflow `φ`: `K` is compact, strictly invariant
(`φᵗ(K) = K` for all `t ≥ 0`), and attracts every bounded set `B`, i.e. for every `ε > 0` the
set `φᵗ(B)` is contained in the `ε`-neighbourhood of `K` for all sufficiently large `t`.
Such a `K` is automatically nonempty.

justification.name: EdensConjecture.IsGlobalAttractor
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of (global) attractor; defined as compact, strictly invariant, and attracting all bounded sets in the Hausdorff semidistance sense.

blocks.name: IsGlobalAttractor
blocks.text:
/-- `K` is the global attractor of the semiflow `φ`: `K` is compact, strictly invariant
(`φᵗ(K) = K` for all `t ≥ 0`), and attracts every bounded set `B`, i.e. for every `ε > 0` the
set `φᵗ(B)` is contained in the `ε`-neighbourhood of `K` for all sufficiently large `t`.
Such a `K` is automatically nonempty. -/
structure IsGlobalAttractor (φ : Flow ℝ≥0 E) (K : Set E) : Prop where
  isCompact : IsCompact K
  image_eq : ∀ t, φ t '' K = K
  attracts : ∀ B : Set E, Bornology.IsBounded B →
    ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ t in atTop, φ t '' B ⊆ thickening ε K

theorem edens_conjecture (φ : Flow ℝ≥0 E) (hφ : ∀ t, ContDiff ℝ 1 (φ t)) (K : Set E)
    (hK : IsGlobalAttractor φ K) :
    ∃ u ∈ K, ((∀ t, φ t u = u) ∨ ∃ T : ℝ≥0, 0 < T ∧ φ T u = u) ∧
      IsMaxOn (localLyapunovDim φ) K u := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Eden's conjecture.** Let `φ` be a smooth dynamical system, i.e. a semiflow
$\{\varphi^t\}_{t \ge 0}$ on a finite-dimensional real inner product space whose time-`t` maps
are continuously differentiable, and let `K` be its global attractor. Then the supremum of the
local Lyapunov dimensions $\dim_{\rm L}^{\rm E}(u)$ over `u ∈ K` is achieved on a stationary
point or on a periodic orbit embedded into `K`: there is `u ∈ K` that is either fixed by every
`φᵗ` or has some period `T > 0`, such that $\dim_{\rm L}^{\rm E}(v) \le \dim_{\rm L}^{\rm E}(u)$
for all `v ∈ K`. The word "unstable" in the original statement is descriptive and is not imposed
as a hypothesis; this keeps the degenerate case in which `K` is itself a stable equilibrium or
cycle.

theorem edens_conjecture (φ : Flow ℝ≥0 E) (hφ : ∀ t, ContDiff ℝ 1 (φ t)) (K : Set E)
    (hK : IsGlobalAttractor φ K) :
    ∃ u ∈ K, ((∀ t, φ t u = u) ∨ ∃ T : ℝ≥0, 0 < T ∧ φ T u = u) ∧
      IsMaxOn (localLyapunovDim φ) K u := by
  sorry

claims.decomposer_note: Single universally quantified existence claim (over smooth finite-dimensional dynamical systems with a compact global attractor K): some u in K that is an equilibrium or lies on a periodic orbit satisfies dim_L(u) = sup_{v in K} dim_L(v), where the local Lyapunov dimension is Eden's infinite-time version (Kaplan–Yorke formula applied to the limsup-of-(omega_d(Dphi^t(u)))^{1/t} local Lyapunov exponents, per Eden 1989 / Kuznetsov arXiv:1602.05410 §on the 'Eden conjecture'); 'unstable' is descriptive and should not be imposed as an extra hypothesis (it would break the degenerate case of an attractor that is itself a stable equilibrium/cycle), the 'or' is one disjunction inside the Prop, and the sup is required to be attained (not merely approached); the article's Kuznetsov–Eden refinement for self-excited/hidden local attractors is a different conjecture not referred to by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: c07 states the conjecture for every C¹ continuous-time semiflow (Mathlib `Flow ℝ≥0 E`, `∀ t, ContDiff ℝ 1 (φ t)`) on a finite-dimensional real inner product space and every global attractor K (compact, strictly invariant, attracts every bounded set — the Temam/Chueshov notion used by the cited Lorenz paper; K nonempty follows since `thickening ε ∅ = ∅`). It asserts ∃ u ∈ K, (stationary ∨ ∃ T > 0, φ T u = u) ∧ IsMaxOn dim_L K u, i.e. genuine attainment, one disjunction, no instability hypothesis. Its local Lyapunov dimension is literally the formula Kuznetsov (arXiv:1602.05410, conclusion) displays for Eden's dim_L^E(u): inf{d ∈ [0,n] : limsup_t ω_d(Dφᵗ(u))^{1/t} < 1} with the value n when the set is empty; ω_d is built from decreasingly sorted eigenvalues of A*A (`LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues` is antitone) with correct 0^0 = 1 conventions, and the limsup lives in [0,∞] so no junk real limsup. My edits: explicit `K`, docstrings on API lemmas, module docstring wording. Rejected: c01/c05/c08 use `ContDiff ℝ ⊤`, which in this Mathlib is `ω` (analytic) — an unintended restriction of 'smooth'; c08 also uses a pointwise/minimal attractor notion; c06 adds an unnecessary `fderiv_bijective` hypothesis and drops joint continuity; c02/c04 use a Kaplan–Yorke-on-integer-partial-sums variant (with 'largest k with Λ_k ≥ 0' / sSup encodings) that can differ from the displayed source formula at irregular points and, for c02, uses a real-valued limsup and `Real.log 0 = 0` junk; c03 is essentially equivalent to c07 but restricted to `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)` with an infDist attraction clause — either would do, c07 is slightly cleaner.

context:
In the mathematics of dynamical systems, Eden's conjecture states that the supremum of the local Lyapunov dimensions on the global attractor is achieved on a stationary point or an unstable periodic orbit embedded into the attractor. 
The validity of the conjecture was proved for a number of well-known systems having global attractor (e.g. for the global attractors in the Lorenz system, complex Ginzburg–Landau equation). It is named after Alp Eden, who proposed it in 1987.

decomposition_objections.text: None of substance. Two remarks: (1) the table's description of the local Lyapunov dimension as 'Kaplan–Yorke formula applied to the limsup-of-ω_d^{1/t} local Lyapunov exponents' is slightly ambiguous; the cited Kuznetsov source states Eden's local dimension explicitly as inf{d : limsup ω_d(Dφᵗ(u))^{1/t} < 1}, which I used (the two readings agree when the defining limits exist, e.g. at equilibria and periodic orbits, and can differ for irregular points). (2) Eden's original conjecture is posed for semiflows on Hilbert spaces (the article cites its verification for the complex Ginzburg–Landau equation), whereas the table restricts to finite-dimensional systems; I conformed to the table.

open Filter Topology Metric
open scoped NNReal

namespace EdensConjecture

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]

/-- The singular values of a linear map `A` on an `n`-dimensional real inner product space, indexed
from `0` and sorted in decreasing order: `singularValue A i` is the square root of the `i`-th
largest eigenvalue of `A* A` for `i < n`, and `0` for `i ≥ n`. -/
noncomputable def singularValue (A : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) (i : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  if h : i < Module.finrank ℝ E then
    Real.sqrt ((LinearMap.isSymmetric_adjoint_mul_self A).eigenvalues rfl ⟨i, h⟩)
  else 0

/-- The singular value function of order `d` of a linear map `A` with singular values
`σ₁ ≥ σ₂ ≥ ⋯ ≥ σₙ`: for `d ∈ [0, n]` it is
`ω_d(A) = σ₁ ⋯ σ_{⌊d⌋} σ_{⌊d⌋ + 1} ^ (d - ⌊d⌋)`, so that `ω_0(A) = 1` and `ω_n(A) = |det A|`. -/
noncomputable def singularValueFunction (A : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) (d : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∏ i ∈ Finset.range ⌊d⌋₊, singularValue A i) * singularValue A ⌊d⌋₊ ^ (d - ⌊d⌋₊)

/-- Singular values are nonnegative. -/
@[category API, AMS 15]
theorem singularValue_nonneg (A : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) (i : ℕ) : 0 ≤ singularValue A i := by
  unfold singularValue
  split_ifs
  · exact Real.sqrt_nonneg _
  · exact le_rfl

/-- The singular value function of order `0` is identically `1`. -/
@[category API, AMS 15]
theorem singularValueFunction_zero (A : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) : singularValueFunction A 0 = 1 := by
  simp [singularValueFunction]

/-- The (infinite-time) local Lyapunov dimension in the sense of Eden of a semiflow `φ` on an
`n`-dimensional space at the point `u`:
$$\dim_{\rm L}^{\rm E}(u) = \inf\{d \in [0, n] :
  \limsup_{t \to +\infty} \big(\omega_d(D\varphi^t(u))\big)^{1/t} < 1\},$$
where `ω_d` is the singular value function and `Dφᵗ(u)` is the derivative of the time-`t` map
at `u`. The `limsup` is taken in `[0, ∞]`. If no `d ∈ [0, n]` satisfies the condition, the
dimension is `n`. -/
noncomputable def localLyapunovDim (φ : Flow ℝ≥0 E) (u : E) : ℝ :=
  sInf {d ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (Module.finrank ℝ E) | d = Module.finrank ℝ E ∨
    limsup (fun t : ℝ≥0 => ENNReal.ofReal
      (singularValueFunction (fderiv ℝ (φ t) u : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) d ^ (1 / (t : ℝ)))) atTop < 1}

/-- The local Lyapunov dimension takes values in `[0, n]`. -/
@[category API, AMS 37]
theorem localLyapunovDim_mem_Icc (φ : Flow ℝ≥0 E) (u : E) :
    localLyapunovDim φ u ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (Module.finrank ℝ E) := by
  have hmem : (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) ∈ {d ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (Module.finrank ℝ E) |
      d = Module.finrank ℝ E ∨ limsup (fun t : ℝ≥0 => ENNReal.ofReal
        (singularValueFunction (fderiv ℝ (φ t) u : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) d ^ (1 / (t : ℝ)))) atTop < 1} :=
    ⟨⟨by positivity, le_rfl⟩, Or.inl rfl⟩
  exact ⟨le_csInf ⟨_, hmem⟩ fun d hd => hd.1.1, csInf_le ⟨0, fun d hd => hd.1.1⟩ hmem⟩

/-- `K` is the global attractor of the semiflow `φ`: `K` is compact, strictly invariant
(`φᵗ(K) = K` for all `t ≥ 0`), and attracts every bounded set `B`, i.e. for every `ε > 0` the
set `φᵗ(B)` is contained in the `ε`-neighbourhood of `K` for all sufficiently large `t`.
Such a `K` is automatically nonempty. -/
structure IsGlobalAttractor (φ : Flow ℝ≥0 E) (K : Set E) : Prop where
  isCompact : IsCompact K
  image_eq : ∀ t, φ t '' K = K
  attracts : ∀ B : Set E, Bornology.IsBounded B →
    ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ t in atTop, φ t '' B ⊆ thickening ε K

/-- **Eden's conjecture.** Let `φ` be a smooth dynamical system, i.e. a semiflow
$\{\varphi^t\}_{t \ge 0}$ on a finite-dimensional real inner product space whose time-`t` maps
are continuously differentiable, and let `K` be its global attractor. Then the supremum of the
local Lyapunov dimensions $\dim_{\rm L}^{\rm E}(u)$ over `u ∈ K` is achieved on a stationary
point or on a periodic orbit embedded into `K`: there is `u ∈ K` that is either fixed by every
`φᵗ` or has some period `T > 0`, such that $\dim_{\rm L}^{\rm E}(v) \le \dim_{\rm L}^{\rm E}(u)$
for all `v ∈ K`. The word "unstable" in the original statement is descriptive and is not imposed
as a hypothesis; this keeps the degenerate case in which `K` is itself a stable equilibrium or
cycle. -/
@[category research open, AMS 37]
theorem edens_conjecture (φ : Flow ℝ≥0 E) (hφ : ∀ t, ContDiff ℝ 1 (φ t)) (K : Set E)
    (hK : IsGlobalAttractor φ K) :
    ∃ u ∈ K, ((∀ t, φ t u = u) ∨ ∃ T : ℝ≥0, 0 < T ∧ φ T u = u) ∧
      IsMaxOn (localLyapunovDim φ) K u := by
  sorry

end EdensConjecture

items: Dynamical system = continuous-time semiflow `Flow ℝ≥0 E` (semigroup property, φ⁰ = id, jointly continuous) on a finite-dimensional real inner product space `E` (n = finrank), with `∀ t, ContDiff ℝ 1 (φ t)` as the 'smooth' hypothesis. Phase space is the whole space (no open subset U), matching the ODE-on-ℝⁿ setting of Kuznetsov 2016 §1. Discrete-time systems (iterated C¹ maps, also treated by Kuznetsov) are not covered by this single declaration; Eden's original infinite-dimensional (Hilbert space / PDE) setting is excluded per the decomposition table's 'finite-dimensional'.
No invertibility of Dφᵗ(u) is assumed (Kuznetsov assumes det J ≠ 0, Eden's framework does not); zero singular values are handled correctly since ω_d = 0 then and 0^(1/t) = 0.

Local Lyapunov dimension uses Kuznetsov's explicit formula for Eden's dim^E_L (arXiv:1602.05410, Conclusion): inf{d ∈ [0,n] : limsup_{t→∞} ω_d(Dφᵗ(u))^{1/t} < 1}, with the source's convention that it equals n if the set is empty (implemented as sInf over {d ∈ [0,n] | d = n ∨ limsup < 1}). This is the ω_d-threshold form of the Kaplan–Yorke formula; it coincides with the Kaplan–Yorke expression on limsup Lyapunov exponents whenever the limits exist (in particular at equilibria and on periodic orbits), and is ≤ it in general. The table's phrase 'Kaplan–Yorke formula applied to the limsup ... exponents' was read in this sense.

The limsup is taken in ℝ≥0∞ via `ENNReal.ofReal` so that an unbounded family yields ∞ (not < 1) rather than a junk real value; the comparison is with the log-free form `< 1` to avoid `Real.log 0 = 0` artifacts.

Singular values: `singularValue A i` = sqrt of the i-th largest eigenvalue of A*A via Mathlib's sorted `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues` (0-indexed, extended by 0 for i ≥ n). ω_d(A) = (∏_{i<⌊d⌋} σ_i) · σ_{⌊d⌋}^{d-⌊d⌋} with `Real.rpow`, so ω_0 = 1, ω_n = |det A| and 0^0 = 1, matching the source's convention.

Global attractor (Temam/Chueshov): compact, strictly invariant (φᵗ(K) = K for all t ≥ 0), and attracts every bounded set (for all ε > 0, φᵗ(B) ⊆ thickening ε K eventually). Nonemptiness of K follows automatically. Stated as a `Prop`-valued structure `IsGlobalAttractor`.
'Achieved' formalized as `IsMaxOn (localLyapunovDim φ) K u`, i.e. u is a maximizer, so the supremum is attained rather than merely approached.

'Stationary point' = `∀ t, φ t u = u`; 'periodic orbit embedded into the attractor' = `∃ T > 0, φ T u = u` with u ∈ K (the orbit lies in K by invariance). 'Unstable' is descriptive and not imposed as a hypothesis, per the decomposition notes; the disjunction is kept even though the periodic case subsumes the stationary one.
Added small API lemmas (`singularValue_nonneg`, `singularValueFunction_zero`, `localLyapunovDim_mem_Icc`) with proofs as basic tests of the bespoke definitions.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities in the original statement and how they were resolved: (1) Class of systems: the table fixes finite-dimensional smooth systems; Eden's original question is for semigroups on Hilbert spaces (the article cites the complex Ginzburg–Landau verification), so the shipped statement is the finite-dimensional special case, as the table directs. Within finite dimensions we take C¹ semiflows (Mathlib `Flow ℝ≥0 E` + `ContDiff ℝ 1 (φ t)`), which contains all ODE-generated systems of Kuznetsov's setup and is the natural reading of 'smooth dynamical system'; discrete-time maps are not covered (the wording 'stationary point' is continuous-time). (2) Local Lyapunov dimension: two conventions exist in the literature — the threshold form inf{d : limsup ω_d(Dφᵗ u)^{1/t} < 1} with real d inside the limsup (displayed by Kuznetsov as Eden's dim_L^E) and the Kaplan–Yorke formula applied to limsup partial sums at integer orders. They coincide whenever the relevant limits exist (equilibria, periodic orbits, regular points) and the threshold value is ≤ the KY value in general. The shipped file uses the threshold form because it is the formula verbatim in the accessible cited primary source. (3) 'Unstable' is treated as descriptive (no hypothesis), 'embedded' is realised by u ∈ K plus strict invariance of K, and attainment is `IsMaxOn`, not approximation. (4) 'Global attractor' = compact, strictly invariant, attracts all bounded sets (Temam/Chueshov, as in the cited Lorenz paper); pointwise/minimal variants (c08) were not used. Boundary cases: finrank 0 gives K = {0}, u = 0 stationary, dim 0 — trivially true; the hypothesis class is nonempty (checked with x ↦ e^{-t}x, K = {0}). Verdict on candidate self-reports: all claimed compile_ok truthfully; c01/c05/c08 did not notice that `⊤` means analytic in current Mathlib.
statement: Eden's conjecture that the supremum of the local Lyapunov dimensions on the global attractor is achieved on a stationary point or an unstable periodic orbit embedded into the attractor.
